words: play; try; idea; together; problem; sketchbook
notes: Play with paint, clay, paper and found things to find ideas, then work with a partner on a small art problem such as a bridge for a toy. Pages go into a first sketchbook. What changes: the first sketchbook is started by play and a partner, with no earlier art work behind it. Assessed by a sketchbook check (three tries on an idea page) and a look-for on the partner work (each child shows the part they added), marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: the first sketchbook is a folder of loose sheets.

words: explore; look closely; research; idea; classmates; sketchbook
notes: Explore materials with classmates, then look closely at a real object or picture and research it by drawing before making a work of art. What changes: looking and drawing a real object now come before making, where kindergarten started from play alone. Assessed by a sketchbook check: a shared-table page with classmates' names and what each tried, and research drawings before the work, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: many ways; partner; question; solve; materials; interest
notes: Come up with many ways, with a partner, to solve one art problem, and follow a personal question into a made work using different materials. What changes: many solutions and a question of the child's own. Assessed by a sketchbook check: at least three solutions with the partner, and the child's own question on the page with the work that follows it, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: imagine; detail; depth; tool; resource; technology
notes: Add detail and depth to a made-up idea, and use the resources, tools and technology on hand to pursue it, such as a free drawing program or paper and a mirror. What changes: ideas get detail and children choose tools. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: brainstorm; goal; group; design problem; maker; plan
notes: Brainstorm several ways to tackle a design problem, then set goals as a group for an artwork that matters to its makers. What changes: the group sets a shared goal and each child brings several routes to it, where grade 3 grew one idea alone. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: merge; fresh idea; research; method; interview; choose
notes: Merge two ideas into a fresh one, and show and name more than one way of researching art (looking, interviewing, sketching, reading) before choosing one to start. What changes: two ideas are merged, and the child names and picks a research method before starting, where grade 4 only listed routes. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: inquiry; question; source; concept; collaborate; plan
notes: Join ideas with classmates to produce fresh ones, and plan an inquiry into content that matters to the student, with a question, sources and a first sketch. What changes: a planned inquiry rather than a single prompt. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: stuck; strategy; guideline; aim; limit; restart
notes: Use strategies to get past being stuck (change the material, set a limit, start from a different edge), and write guidelines to steer a work toward a stated aim. What changes: strategies for being stuck and written guidelines. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: record; process; inquiry; contemporary; daily life; medium
notes: Keep a record of early creative steps as pictures or words in an old or new medium, and with a group shape a question about modern daily life that draws on current art or design. What changes: the record of early steps is kept as it happens, and the group inquiry looks at the present day, not a past style. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: route; start; inquiry; contemporary; practice; design
notes: Start one project three ways (a word web, a thumbnail page, a photo walk), pick the strongest, and frame a question about daily life today that a current artist or designer has also taken up. What changes: the student tries several start routes and frames a question about daily life through current practice, with no teacher-set prompt as in grade 8. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 1 bridge: the first unit teaches the grade 8 techniques and words Level 1 needs, as readiness, and claims no grade 8 id (at most 12 days in the full year, 6 on the 80-day short path, STANDARD.md 3.2).

words: pose; problem; earlier work; select; method; plan
notes: Pick a problem left open in an earlier piece of the student's own, alone or with a partner, and fill a planning page that weighs two or three materials and methods, old and new, before choosing. What changes: problems come from the student's own earlier work. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 2 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: predict; social change; series; theme; norm; material
notes: Plan art or design that could move a community toward a change, and plan a themed series that follows or breaks a norm on purpose, using old and new materials. What changes: the plan carries a social aim and runs as a series, where level 2 planned single pieces from the student's own earlier work. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 3 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: experiment; paint; clay; safe; non-toxic; tool
notes: Experiment with paint, clay, crayon and paper to build skill, and pick safe, non-toxic supplies and tools with the teacher. What changes: the first hands on tools: experiment with media and pick safe supplies with the teacher. Assessed by a guide look-for on the kept experiment sheets and a safe-supply pick: from a tray of items or picture cards (labeled non-toxic against unlabeled, blunt against sharp) the child picks the safe ones and says why, marked as met, partly or not yet. Handling is practice here (grade 1's id). Teacher note: only supplies labeled non-toxic; no small items in the mouth; scissors and glue shown before use.

words: try; tool; material; safe; handle; clean up
notes: Try what materials and tools can do, and show the safe grip and handling for each tool before using it for real work. What changes: the child shows safe handling aloud and in action before using a tool, where kindergarten picked supplies with the teacher. Assessed by a look-for on the kept practice sheet and a table item: the child shows and tells one tool's safe grip and handling, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: show and practise each tool's safe grip before the first use.

words: choose; interest; clean; studio; tool; gear
notes: Spend a choice day with paper, clay and paint on an interest of the child's own, then lead a partner through the clean-up card: brushes washed, tools back, table wiped. What changes: a personal choice of material and cleaning as part of the job. Assessed by a look-for on the choice-day work and a table item: the child cleans one tool and puts it back by the clean-up card's steps, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: process; printing; collage; modeling; finish; skilled
notes: Make a finished artwork the child is happy with, using more than one process and material, and show safe, skilled handling across the processes (for example printing, collage and modeling). What changes: one finished work now crosses several processes, where grade 2 tried materials one at a time. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique.

words: technique; invent; care; equipment; safe; hurt
notes: Test a set of mark-making tools on a sample sheet, invent one technique of the student's own and name it, and pass a tool check before using scissors or other sharp tools. What changes: inventing techniques and a duty of care to others. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique. Teacher note: sharp tools only after a safe-handling check.

words: practice; skill; craft; care; log; technique
notes: Build skill in several techniques through experiments and practice logged in the sketchbook, and show fine craft by caring for and using supplies and tools well. What changes: practice is logged and craft means care. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique.

words: open; new method; environment; waste; reuse; cleanup
notes: Show openness to new ideas, materials and methods, and explain how saving, caring for and cleaning up supplies affects the environment (waste, rinse water, reuse). What changes: the student explains the environmental cost of waste and rinse water, where grade 5 judged craft by care alone. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence.

words: persist; skill; online; permission; share; duty
notes: Work one piece through several sessions in two or more media, keeping a process log of what was tried and fixed, and plan how a photo of it would be shared online with permission and no faces or names. What changes: persistence is shown over weeks and sharing carries duty. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence.

words: risk; invent; copyright; fair use; open license; borrow
notes: Take a planned risk in one piece (a new medium, scale or subject) and log what it meant to the work, then label each borrowed image in the piece as own, open license or public domain, with credit. What changes: the student takes a risk with an idea and explains how copyright and open licenses apply to own work, where grade 7 attended to sharing images. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence. Teacher note: only public domain or openly licensed sources are used as models in the unit.

words: unplanned; material; hazard; health; ventilation; safety
notes: Make an artwork or design without planning it first, to learn what the materials do, and explain how materials can affect people's health and nature while handling them safely. What changes: the student makes without planning first to learn what a material does, and explains its health and nature effects, with the hazard sheet read before use. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons. Teacher note: a hazard sheet for each material is read before use; ventilation and cleanup are shown.

words: persistence; skill; ethics; consent; credit; documentation
notes: Show gained skill and knowledge in the student's art form through experiments and persistence documented over a term, and show understanding of the ethics of making and sharing creative work (credit, consent, cultural care). What changes: skill growth is documented over a term, and the ethics of making and sharing (credit, consent, cultural care) are reasoned, not just followed. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons.

words: theme; series; liberty; duty; image; ethics
notes: Try ideas, plan and make several works on a theme that matters to the student, and weigh liberty against duty when using and sharing images, materials and tools. What changes: a theme across several works and a reasoned view on freedom and duty. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons.

words: place; tree; building; story; my life; draw
notes: Make art that shows the natural and built places around the child, such as a tree, a school or a street, and tell a story from the child's own life in a picture. What changes: first art that shows places and a story from the child's own life. Assessed by a product check: the finished piece and a short talk, marked on a three-line guide. Teacher note: invite stories, never require a private one.

words: sort; object; use; diagram; sculpture; reasons
notes: Sort everyday objects by what they are used for in drawings, diagrams or sculpture, and name when, where and why people make art beyond school. What changes: objects are sorted by use, and art is placed beyond school. Assessed by a product check: the sort shown as labeled groups, with any sculpture beside it, on a three-line guide, and a talk item on one time, place and reason for art beyond school.

words: reuse; transform; object; event; community; new use
notes: Turn a cast-off object (a box, a lid, a sock) into something with a new use, and make a picture that tells about an event at home, at school or in the neighborhood. What changes: reuse and a community event as subject. Assessed by a product check: the finished piece and a short talk, marked on a three-line guide.

words: model; map; diagram; place; observe; scale
notes: Alone or together, make a model, diagram or map of a familiar place, and make an artwork drawn from what the child sees around them. What changes: models and maps of a real place. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: region; record; depict; building; place; look closely
notes: Record and depict built places in the region by looking at them, and describe what you recorded. What changes: places are recorded from observation of the real thing, where grade 3 mapped places from memory. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: place; object; matters; record; vocabulary; symmetry
cross_subject: math:4.G.A.3 (finding lines of symmetry in a design)
notes: Draw a map or a set of sketches of places and objects that matter to the student, labeled with art and design words, and use the labels to point out one thing never noticed before. What changes: choosing what matters and using the vocabulary. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: user; need; rework; system; design; interest
notes: Create or rework an object, place or system for the stated needs of named users, and note what each user needs, starting from a collection of ideas drawn from current interests and concerns, with a public or invented option marked the same. What changes: a design is made for named users and their stated needs, not for the maker's taste. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: hierarchy; layout; contrast; scale; information; gather
cross_subject: math:7.G.A.1 (a scale drawing of a layout)
notes: Apply visual organizing strategies (hierarchy, grouping, scale, contrast) to make work that clearly shares information, and make a visual record (a map, sketches or photos with no faces) of where and when people gather for art in the community. What changes: a design job is now organizing information so a viewer reads it clearly, where grade 6 met the needs of users. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: layout; text; image; presentation; group identity; audience
notes: Pick and arrange pictures and text so a presentation is clear and compelling to an audience, and make art with a group that reflects on and strengthens the good side of a group's identity (the class, the school, a team or an invented group). What changes: pictures and text are arranged together for an audience, where grade 7 organized information alone. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: propose; space; experience; develop; spark; model
notes: With a small team, sketch and model a change to one school space that would alter how people move or feel there, and keep an idea log from first sketch to final proposal. What changes: the student proposes a change to one place with others, drawn and modeled, and records how an idea grew, where grade 8 made art together without a site. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary. Teacher note: proposals are drawings and models; nothing is built on school grounds without permission.

words: rework; issue; research; investigate; experiment; system
notes: Redesign an object, a routine or a place in answer to a current issue, and keep a research page of what was observed, read and tested while making it. What changes: an issue drives the redesign and research is documented. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary.

words: culture; image; object; society; history; argument
notes: Make a work about how one culture's images or objects help or hinder people's lives, with a research page that ties the making to the history, the society and the student's own experience. What changes: art is used to argue a view and back it with named sources, where level 2 reworked things in answer to an issue. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary. Teacher note: sources are named and sensitive subjects get a reading by a second adult before the work is shown.

words: tell; make; choose; color; shape; mix
notes: Tell how the child makes art as the child works, using pictures and a few words ('I mixed blue and yellow'). What changes: the first telling: the child says aloud how they make art as they work. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: describe the making, never grade the picture.

words: line; shape; color; texture; choice; art word
notes: Use art words to tell the choices made while making art (color, line, shape, texture). What changes: the child uses art words for choices, where kindergarten used everyday words. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: classmate; ask; answer; choice; talk; turn
notes: Talk with classmates about the choices made while making an artwork, taking turns to ask a question and answer it. What changes: the child holds a two-way talk with a classmate about choices, where grade 1 named choices alone. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: detail; meaning; strengthen; partner; add; change
cross_subject: ela:SL.3.1 (taking part in a collaborative talk with a partner)
notes: Add detail to an artwork to strengthen the meaning that is appearing, after a short talk with a partner. What changes: the child changes the work to strengthen its meaning. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: critique; feedback; revise; step; group; change
notes: Change an artwork in progress using ideas from classmate talk in a small-group critique with set steps. What changes: a protocol with steps and a revision made from the talk. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: artist statement; explain; choice; revise; art words; critique
notes: Write an artist statement that uses art words to explain choices, then revise the work and the statement after a critique. What changes: the child writes an artist statement, where grade 4 spoke in a critique. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: intent; viewer; match; revise; critique; message
notes: Check whether an artwork gets across what was meant, using a critique and a viewer's retelling, and change it to match. What changes: intent is compared with what viewers see. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change.

words: reflect; key point; statement; format; explain; evidence
notes: Reflect on a work and explain its key points in a statement or another way (a recorded talk or a labeled sketch). What changes: the child picks the format of the reflection (a statement, a recorded talk or a labeled sketch). Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change.

words: standard; examine; unfinished; plan; revise; criteria
notes: Use fitting standards to examine and think over unfinished art, then plan changes in writing before making them. What changes: named standards guide the examination of unfinished work and changes are planned in writing before they are made. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change. Teacher note: critique is of the work, never of the person.

words: standard; culture; review; revise; unfinished; past
notes: Use standards from past and present cultures to review and revise unfinished art, naming whose standards are used. What changes: the review uses standards from more than one culture and names whose they are. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: critique; reflect; rework; polish; vision; draft
notes: After a classmate critique, reflect, rework and polish a work toward the student's own vision, keeping the draft and final side by side. What changes: the student's vision, not only the standards, sets the aim. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: revisit; polish; standard; vision; defend; statement
notes: Revisit and polish art or design with old and new standards and the student's vision, and defend the changes in a short statement. What changes: every change made after the review is defended with a reason, where level 2 polished toward the student's vision. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: choose; collection; keep; display; favorite; why
notes: Pick three of the child's own works for a small collection folder, say why each one went in, and tell the class why people keep a collection. What changes: first choosing of objects to keep and show. Assessed by a product check: the child shows three chosen pieces and says why each, marked on a three-line guide, and a talk item on why people keep a collection. Teacher note: the child's collection is of the child's own choosing; the teacher keeps a folder of the child's work.

words: prize; ready; show; where; when; how
notes: Explain why people prize certain objects and artworks, and ask and answer when, where and how to get a work ready to show. What changes: the child asks and answers when, where and how to prepare a work for showing, where kindergarten only chose. Assessed by a talk item on why people prize a work, and the kept exhibit-plan card (when, where, how) scored with the mounted piece on a three-line guide.

words: theme; group; exhibit; mount; label; display
notes: Group artworks around a shared theme for an exhibit, and tell apart the materials or ways used to get work ready for display (mounting, labels, frames). What changes: works are grouped by theme and the display materials (mounting, labels, frames) are told apart. Assessed by a product check: the piece placed in its theme group and why it fits, on a three-line guide, and a kept card matching a mount, a label and a frame to what each does.

words: space; online; gallery; artist note; choose; ready
notes: Walk the room, the hallway and a class web page as possible show spaces and list what each can and cannot do, then choose one, mount the work and write a short artist note for it. What changes: a chosen space and a written artist note. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: technology; keep; guard; format; preserve; change
notes: Compare a museum's old and new ways of keeping and showing art from pictures and a short video, and plan how the class's own work is shown and protected in two places, such as a wall and a slideshow. What changes: technology across time is weighed, where grade 3 chose a space and wrote a note. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: curator; care; role; safe; prepare; argue
notes: Take the curator's job for a small class show: list the care and display jobs, then argue for one set of safe materials and one way of mounting the work, with reasons. What changes: a named role and an argument with reasons. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: flat; 3D; digital; display plan; viewer; layout
notes: Compare how flat, three-dimensional and digital art are kept and shown, and draw a display plan, alone or in a group, that fits space, viewers and layout. What changes: a drawn display plan replaces a talk about spaces. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons.

words: compare; technology; standard; judge; method; viewing
notes: Compare how a work is kept and seen in a gallery, in print and on a screen, then score two ways of preparing the class's work for showing against a set checklist. What changes: methods of preparing and showing are judged against standards, where grade 6 drew a plan. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons.

words: standard; group show; theme; exhibition story; viewer; select
notes: Write the standards for picking a themed group of works, then with a team hang the show and write the wall stories viewers read. What changes: a group show goes up with written stories for its viewers, not a plan alone. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons. Teacher note: a showing outside class needs each family's yes.

words: curate; analyze; exhibition; keep; choose; judge
notes: Choose and arrange works for a small show and for keeping, and write a short note on why a real exhibition is laid out the way it is. What changes: the student acts as curator and critic of a whole show, where grade 8 only planned one with a group. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: portfolio; select; critique; site; method; show
notes: Choose and critique the student's own works for a portfolio show, and pick hanging and lighting methods that suit one named place. What changes: the student's own portfolio and a site-specific plan. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: curate; present; justify; event; conservation; protect
notes: Curate and hang a show for an exhibit or event, with a written reason for each choice, and compare two ways the works could be stored and protected afterward. What changes: choices are justified for a public event and conservation is researched, where level 2 sited the student's own portfolio. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: museum; art; building; visit; look; for
notes: Look at pictures of an art museum beside an ordinary building and tell what is different inside, and tell what one artwork in it is for. What changes: the first idea of a museum and of an artwork's use. Assessed by a kept sort (museum, store and house pictures, with one difference told) and a talk item on what one artwork is for, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: a class visit, or a virtual visit with a museum's own free pages.

words: museum; job; visitor; reason; long ago; place
notes: Act out the jobs people do at a museum (guard, guide, visitor), then look at artworks from two times or places and give a reason each was made. What changes: museum jobs are named, and several reasons for making art replace one. Assessed by a kept job-card sort (acting is practice, never needed for the mark) and a talk item on one reason each of two works was made, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: community; public art; culture; era; compare; use
notes: Explain how art shown in a museum or a public square helps a community, and compare how two cultures used art in different times and places. What changes: two cultures' uses of art are set side by side, where grade 1 listed reasons. Assessed by two talk items: one way public or museum art helps a community, and one likeness and one difference between two cultures' uses, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: story; history; record; setting; time; place
notes: Study artworks that tell a story or record history from more than one culture, and say how the student's first reaction changed after learning when and where one was made. What changes: art as story and record, and setting changes a reaction. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: gallery; aim; experience; infer; clue; culture; tradition; community
notes: Compare what a museum, a gallery and a community center offer visitors, infer from clues when, where and in what culture a work was made, and make a piece that shows a community tradition taken from a community source. What changes: setting is inferred from clues, and a community tradition is shown only from a source the community offers. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: evidence; show; topic; belief; value; change
notes: Show from a real exhibit or its pages how it carries an idea or information on a topic, and describe how art can change what people believe, value or do. What changes: the student points to evidence in a real exhibit, not just describes what museums do. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: community; history; value; mirror; custom; era
cross_subject: social-studies:ss6-paleolithic-neolithic (cave art studied with its time and place)
notes: Study a local or online museum and judge, with evidence, how it shows its community's history and values, and trace how art changed with the era, the customs and the materials on hand. What changes: a museum is judged with evidence, where grade 5 pointed to evidence in one exhibit. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: venue; collection; setting; supplies; reaction; compare
notes: Compare what it is like to view collections and exhibits in different venues, and analyze how knowing a work's era, place, supplies and uses shapes the way people react to it. What changes: the student compares what it is like to see an exhibit in different venues, and how knowing a work's era, place and use changes a reaction. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: influence; belief; collection; group identity; represent; mirror
notes: Study one exhibition or collection and explain how it shapes what visitors think and believe, then sort a set of works by how each shows, builds or reflects a group's identity. What changes: art is tied to group identity, where grade 7 compared venues. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: exhibit; society; politics; culture; custom; reaction
notes: Analyze how an exhibit shapes awareness of society, culture and politics, and describe how knowing a culture, its customs and history can change a viewer's reaction to a work. What changes: politics and society now enter the analysis of an exhibit, where grade 8 looked at group identity. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: history; link; defend; society; local; compare
notes: Write an argument that ties a set of artworks to the history, culture and politics around them, and compare how art was used in two past societies with how it is used locally now. What changes: links are argued and defended, where level 1 only analyzed how an exhibit shaped awareness. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: curate; collection; influence; belief; society; experience
notes: Curate a small collection, real or on paper, that helps viewers understand one social, cultural or political experience, and write a judgment of how an artist or group changed what a society believed or did. What changes: the student builds the collection and judges influence on a society, where level 2 defended links. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: a collection on a sensitive subject is read by a second adult before it is shown. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: picture; show; look; see; art; around us
notes: Find the art in the child's surroundings and tell what it is used for, and tell what a picture shows, using look and tell routines on photos and paintings. What changes: first looking: find nearby art and its use, and say what a picture shows. Assessed by two talk items: what one nearby work of art is used for, and what an unseen picture shows, each marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: use images with plain subjects first.

words: everyday; compare; same; different; subject; describe
notes: Choose artworks that show everyday life and describe them to a partner, then compare two pictures of the same subject side by side. What changes: two pictures of one subject are compared, where kindergarten described one. Assessed by two talk items: picking and describing a picture of everyday life, and comparing two pictures of one subject, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: feeling; sort; mood; nature; building; describe
notes: Go on a looking walk outside and in the building and describe what the child sees and feels, then sort a set of pictures into piles by the feeling each gives. What changes: feelings become a way to sort pictures, where grade 1 compared by subject. Assessed by two talk items: how a photographed place looks and feels, and a sort of unseen pictures by feeling with a reason, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: guess; clue; process; message; picture; because
notes: Play art detective: find clues in an artwork to guess how it was made, then work out the message the picture sends. What changes: guessing process and message from evidence in the picture. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide.

words: before; after; part; message; image; reaction
notes: Write a first reaction to an artwork, make a small piece like it, write a second reaction, and compare the two, then mark the parts of an image that carry its message. What changes: parts of the image are named as carriers of a message. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide.

words: reading; others; culture; link; image; compare
notes: Compare your own reading of an artwork with how others read it, and find and analyze cultural links a picture suggests. What changes: other readings are weighed, and culture becomes a clue in the picture. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: interpret; persuade; culture; visual part; feeling; action
notes: Interpret art and design from more than one part of the world that shows how people live and what they value, and mark the visual parts and cultural ties that steer a viewer's ideas and feelings. What changes: the student analyzes how visual parts and cultural links sway ideas, feelings and actions, where grade 5 only found the links. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: audience; display; location; value; sway; image
notes: Explain how the way a work is displayed, where it is and the viewer's own experience change how it is seen and valued, and analyze several ways images sway different audiences. What changes: display and audience join the picture as things that change meaning. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric.

words: taste; culture; setting; media; sway; image
notes: Explain from examples how culture and surroundings shape what people like and how they see themselves, and compare where viewers meet images that try to sway them (a billboard, a feed, a gallery). What changes: settings and media are compared, where grade 7 looked at audiences. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: perceive; experience; image; view; analyze; world
notes: Write a short proposal on how one set of artworks shapes how people understand a human experience, and reflect on how images seen every day shape the student's own view. What changes: the student looks at their own seeing, where grade 8 compared settings. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning.

words: taste; surroundings; audience; judge; image; feeling
notes: Keep a page of reactions to natural and built places, then judge how well a set of images sways a named audience's ideas, feelings and actions. What changes: the student judges how well an image works on its audience, where level 1 analyzed how images shape a viewer. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning.

words: reaction; growth; pattern; era; type; share
notes: Analyze how a reaction to art grows with learning and life experience, and find what artists or images of one type, era or culture have in common. What changes: patterns across a type, era or culture are found, where level 2 judged single images. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: subject; detail; prefer; because; meaning; like
notes: Look at an artwork with the class, name what it shows and point to the details, and tell which of two artworks the child likes more and why. Use the sentence 'I like it because'. What changes: first judging: name a subject and key details, and say why you prefer one work. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: subject; form; sort; reason; feature; prefer
notes: Sort what is in an artwork and name its lines, shapes and colors to work out its meaning, then sort a set of artworks by the reasons people give for liking them. What changes: features of form are named and several reasons for liking a work are sorted, where kindergarten gave one reason. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: mood; subject; form; prefer; art word; meaning
notes: Find an artwork's meaning from the mood it suggests, its subject and its form, and use art words to say which work the child prefers. What changes: mood joins subject and form as a source of meaning, where grade 1 sorted by subject and features of form. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: media; mood; standard; judge; given; meaning
notes: Study how an artist's materials build the subject and mood of a work to say what it means, then judge it with the teacher's checklist. What changes: standards given by the teacher are applied for the first time, where grade 2 gave a preference in art words. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: background; context; standard; judge; compare; meaning
notes: Read a short background card on an artwork, study its subject, form and media to say what it means, and judge two artworks with one checklist. What changes: background facts feed the meaning, and one set of standards is used on more than one work. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: structure; context; genre; standard; culture; mood
notes: Study an artwork's form, structure, setting, subject and media to find its ideas and mood, and compare how people judge art differently across styles, times and cultures. What changes: the student describes how standards for judging art change with style, history and culture. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: context; evidence; standard; create; judge; useful
cross_subject: ela:W.6.1 (a claim with reasons and evidence)
notes: Sort useful from unhelpful context before studying a work, and create and use fitting standards to judge an artwork. What changes: the student creates standards and uses an evidence sentence. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: taste; standard; weigh; making; evidence; judge
notes: Weigh how a work was made, its form, setting, subject and media to say what it means, then judge it twice, once by personal taste and once by set standards, and explain the difference. What changes: personal taste and established standards are told apart, where grade 6 made standards for a work. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: argue; reasons; judgment; context; structure; message
cross_subject: ela:W.8.1 (an argument supported by reasons and evidence)
notes: Write an analysis of how subject, form, media, approach and setting together build a work's message and mood, and argue for a judgment of it with solid reasons. What changes: the judgment is argued in writing with solid reasons, where grade 7 compared taste and standards. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: evidence; context; standards; collection; explain; cite
notes: Write an interpretation of an artwork backed with evidence from the piece and its setting, and draft the standards a jury would use to judge that work or a collection. What changes: evidence is counted for enough, and the student sets standards for a work or collection. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

words: background; interpretation; source; standards; fit; decide
notes: List the background facts that change how an artwork is read, then test how well two other people's judging standards fit one work or collection. What changes: other people's standards are tested against a work, and background that helps interpretation is named. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

words: interpretation; compete; defend; believable; standards; judgment
notes: Lay out competing readings of an artwork and defend the most believable, then judge one work or collection by several different sets of standards. What changes: competing interpretations are weighed against each other and several sets of standards are used in one judgment. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

model_in: sketchbook; safe-studio; practice-log; talk-about-choices; critique-protocol; artist-statement
model_out: sketchbook; safe-studio; practice-log; talk-about-choices; critique-protocol; artist-statement
words: self-directed; series; proposal; studio; revision; portfolio
notes: Level 4 is an optional year the student leads: a self-directed series built from a written proposal, with planning, making and revision repeated on new work. Assessed by a portfolio of the series and a defended artist statement, scored on the same rubric as Level 3 with a higher bar for independence. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new, self-chosen work.

words: liberty; duty; image; culture; society; project
notes: The student takes on one project that uses art or design to speak to a real audience, and keeps a record of choices about materials, sources, consent and sharing. Assessed by the finished project and a written account of its ethical choices. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to a new project.

words: curate; exhibit; justify; conservation; society; catalog
notes: The student curates and presents a small public exhibit from the Level 4 work, writing a justified label for each piece and a plan for protecting the work. Assessed by the exhibition, the labels and a short talk to visitors, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: a showing outside class needs each family's yes. A student of 18 or over gives their own yes to be shown; otherwise the family does. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11.

words: interpretation; criticism; compare; believable; standards; evidence
cross_subject: ela:W.11-12.1 (an argument with valid reasoning and evidence)
notes: The student writes an extended critical essay comparing the interpretations of a work or group of works, defending the most believable one with evidence and more than one set of standards. Assessed by the essay and a defended talk, scored on a rubric. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new works.

words: beat; high; low; sound; motif; move
notes: Explore beat and the shape of a tune by moving, singing and tapping, then invent short motifs from movement. Ideas go into a first idea bank, a bundle of recordings or picture cards. What changes: first year: beat and tune shape are felt by moving, singing and tapping, and a first motif is invented. Assessed by a music-making check: the teacher marks each child's tries as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: the child's voice is never forced; a clap, a tap or a found sound counts.

words: favorite; pick; picture symbol; record; order; idea
notes: Choose a favorite sound idea from a class game and keep it as a row of picture symbols or a short recording. What changes: first year: ideas are picked and kept, not yet explained. Assessed by a kept-ideas check: the teacher marks each child's picked and kept ideas as met, partly or not yet.

words: feedback; improve; share; classmates; finished; again
notes: Use help from self, peers and teacher to improve a musical idea, then play a finished version for classmates. What changes: first year: one idea is improved with help and played for classmates. Assessed by a sharing check: the teacher marks the change and the sharing as met, partly or not yet.

words: high; low; loud; soft; same; different
notes: Notice high and low, loud and soft, and same and different in songs, and show each with the body. What changes: first year: high and low, loud and soft, and same and different are shown with the body, with no notation. Assessed by a listening game: the teacher marks each child's body answers as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: beat counts and body answers only, no note values.

words: loud; soft; fast; slow; voice; mean
notes: Sing a song loud and soft, fast and slow, and say which way fits its words best, then hear a performer do the same and point out the change. What changes: first year: voice, loudness and speed are noticed as carriers of what a maker means. Assessed by a listen-and-show check: the teacher marks each child's answers as met, partly or not yet.

words: practice; again; feedback; expressive; audience; sing
notes: Use help from self, teacher and peers to improve a performance, try suggested ways to practice, and perform expressively for an audience such as the class. What changes: first year: a performance is improved with help and given to an audience such as the class. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher marks each child's performance as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: volume stays low, no child is made to sing alone, and a group or recorded version is always an option.

words: favorite; like; choose; why; song; interest
notes: Bring a song the child likes (or pick one from the class list), tell the class what is good about it, and tell how what the child likes or knows shaped a choice (a song, or a way to sing it), with a story character's choice as an option marked the same. What changes: first year: what interests a child is shown and said. Assessed by a favorites check: the teacher marks each child's show-and-say as met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; tune; like; judge; art; school
notes: Move to the beat or show the tune going up and down while a piece plays, say whether the child likes it, and name a story, picture or game the music goes with. What changes: first year: a music idea is shown and a taste is stated. Assessed by a listen-and-say check: the teacher marks each child's answers as met, partly or not yet.

words: reply; phrase; purpose; major; minor; twos and threes
notes: Make a reply phrase for a purpose such as a greeting or a goodnight, and try ideas that sound happy or sad and that move in twos or threes. What changes: a purpose for each idea and a first try at different tonalities and meters. Assessed by a music-making check: the teacher marks each child's phrases as met, partly or not yet.

words: choose; reason; notation; recording; picture symbols; express
notes: Play ideas chosen to express an intent, say why they were chosen, and document them in picture or standard notation or in a recording. What changes: the child gives a reason and documents the idea. Assessed by a kept-ideas check: the teacher marks the reason and the record as met, partly or not yet.

words: feedback; polish; purpose; meaning; share; change
notes: Play or sing a short idea for a partner and the teacher, change one thing after their feedback, then share the finished music and say what it is for. What changes: the child polishes with less help and says what the music is for. Assessed by a sharing check: the teacher marks the change and the purpose as met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; melody direction; picture notation; rhythm; culture; pattern
notes: Show the beat and which way a tune moves in music from many cultures, and read and perform short rhythm patterns in picture or standard notation. Beat counts and picture symbols only, no note values. What changes: reading begins with simple rhythm patterns from picture symbols. Assessed by a read-and-play task scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: music from a culture is chosen from that community's own published teaching or a named practitioner. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: loudness; speed; express; creator; performer; show
notes: Sing one song in two ways (loud and soft, fast and slow) and tell which fits what the song means, then name the choice a recorded performer made. What changes: the child names how loudness and speed carry what a creator means, where kindergarten only noticed them. Assessed by a listen-and-show check scored on a three-line guide.

words: rehearse; strategy; expressive; purpose; audience; feedback
notes: Use feedback from self, teacher and peers to improve a performance, try a suggested rehearsal strategy on a hard spot, and perform expressively in a way that fits both the audience and the purpose. What changes: less help, and a performance fitted to an audience and a purpose. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher marks each child's performance as met, partly or not yet.

words: interest; purpose; experience; choose; skill; knowledge
notes: Pick a piece from a short listening menu for a purpose such as a lullaby or a march, tell why, and tell how what the child likes, knows or can do shaped the pick, with a public or story-character option marked the same. What changes: choices are tied to a purpose for the music, where kindergarten only showed interest. Assessed by a favorites check with one spoken reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; pitch; purpose; style; judge; connect
notes: Listen to pieces in different styles and show with the body where the beat or the pitch does its job, say which the child likes for a given purpose, and link one piece to a story, a picture or a school subject. What changes: the child names a purpose that beat or pitch serves, where kindergarten only showed an idea. Assessed by a listen-and-say check, marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: improvise; pattern; rhythm; melody; tonality; meter
notes: Improvise rhythm and melody patterns for a purpose, then make patterns inside a tonality and meter the teacher gives. What changes: improvising on purpose and working inside a given tonality and meter. Assessed by a performance of two patterns scored on a three-line guide.

words: combine; sequence; document; notation; recording; order
notes: Show and explain why patterns were chosen, then document, combine and sequence ideas in picture or standard notation or a recording. What changes: ideas are combined and put in order, not only kept one by one. Assessed by a documented short piece scored on a three-line guide.

words: feedback; revise; sense; mean; for; share
notes: Play a short piece for self, partner and teacher feedback, choose which advice to use and revise, then share the finished music and tell what it means and what it is for. What changes: the child decides which feedback to use. Assessed by a revised piece and a one-line note on the change, scored on a three-line guide.

words: tonality; meter; major; minor; rhythm pattern; melody pattern
notes: Learn songs from more than one culture and show whether each is major or minor and moves in twos or threes, then read and play rhythm and melody patterns from picture or standard notation. Rhythms are taught by beat counts and a spoken counting system. What changes: tonality and meter are named, and melody patterns are read as well as rhythms. Assessed by a read-and-play task scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: tempo; dynamics; concept; intent; creator; performer
notes: Perform a song with planned loud, soft, fast and slow parts, then listen to two performers and say how each one's choices show what the music means. What changes: qualities beyond loudness and speed are tied to a creator's intent. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a three-line guide.

words: criteria; accurate; expressive; effective; strategy; rehearse
notes: Score a class performance with a short checklist, practice one hard spot with a named strategy such as slow, then up to speed, and perform for a purpose such as a morning song. What changes: the child chooses the strategy and judges with set criteria. Assessed by a performance scored on a three-line guide (accurate, expressive, fits the purpose).

words: interest; purpose; explain; choose; knowledge; varied
notes: Choose music for a class purpose from a listening menu and explain the pick, and tell how something the child likes or has done shapes the choice. What changes: the child explains a choice in words, where grade 1 showed and discussed it. Assessed by a short spoken or written reason scored on a three-line guide.

words: concept; purpose; judge; taste; connect; subject
notes: Listen for how a piece's beat, tune or speed suits its purpose, judge it for that purpose by taste and expression, and connect it to another art or a school subject. What changes: the child describes how a music concept serves a purpose, where grade 1 only showed it. Assessed by a short listen-and-describe response scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: improvise; setting; purpose; choose; fits; tonality
notes: Improvise rhythm and melody ideas, say how they fit a purpose and a setting, then invent ideas in a tonality or meter the child chooses. What changes: the child explains the fit and chooses the tonality or meter. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a short rubric.

words: piece; purpose; rhythm; melody; standard notation; picture notation
notes: Make up a short piece for a purpose (a game song, a goodnight tune) and write its rhythm and melody in picture or standard notation, or record it. What changes: ideas become a piece with a stated purpose. Assessed by a documented piece, played with its purpose said, scored on a short rubric.

words: criteria; judge; record; changes; audience; intent
notes: Improve a class piece with a checklist the teacher and class set, mark the changes on the page, and share it with an audience, saying how it shows what the child meant. What changes: class criteria guide the changes and an audience hears the result. Assessed by a revised piece with a recorded change list, shared with an audience with its intent described, scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; section; rhythm; short tune; notation; context
cross_subject: math:3.NF.A.1 (a note value is a part of a whole bar)
notes: Map the form of a song the class will perform, read and play its rhythms and short tune from picture and standard notation, and talk about how where and why people sing it shapes the performance. Note values are placed after the unit on fractions as parts of a whole. What changes: whole tunes are read in picture and standard notation, and the setting of a performance is described. Assessed by a form map, a read-and-play task and a written description of the setting, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: reading; interpret; loudness; speed; intent; performer
notes: Try a song with different loudness and speed and pick the version that carries its meaning, then describe how a recorded performer uses the same tools. What changes: the child compares readings by different performers, where grade 2 named qualities in one. Assessed by a performance and a short description scored on a short rubric.

words: ensemble; criteria; polish; manners; audience; venue
notes: Score a class ensemble take for accuracy with a shared checklist, rehearse the weak spots, and perform for an audience with the manners of a performer and a listener. What changes: ensemble work, class criteria and audience manners. Assessed by a performance, a take judged on class criteria and a self-check, with performer and audience manners observed, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a solo or doubled version is always offered.

words: setting; purpose; choose; reflect; knowledge; audience
notes: Choose a piece for the class to perform and present the reasons (what it is for, where it will be sung, what the class knows), and tell how it fits the student's own interests. What changes: setting joins interest and purpose as a reason for choosing music to perform. Assessed by a listening-log entry with a reason scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; element; setting; criteria; fit; connect
cross_subject: ela:SL.3.1 (class talk about what was heard)
notes: Listen to a piece, describe how its form, its elements and where it is heard shape the student's response, score it with a set checklist, and connect it to another art or subject. What changes: set criteria and the personal or social setting enter the judging, where grade 2 judged by taste and expression. Assessed by a listen-and-describe response scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: harmony; accompaniment; related; explain; setting; drone
notes: Improvise rhythms and tunes with a simple harmony part over a drone, say how they fit a stated purpose, and make up a short accompaniment in a given key and meter. What changes: harmony and accompaniment join rhythm and melody. Assessed by a performance with a spoken reason, scored on a short rubric.

words: arrange; compose; organized; context; harmony; notation
notes: Play ideas chosen and organized for improvising, arranging or composing, say what each is for, and write down rhythm, melody and a simple harmony part. What changes: organizing and explaining join documenting, and simple harmony is written down, where grade 3 documented one melody. Assessed by a documented piece and a spoken or written reason, scored on a rubric.

words: growth; shared criteria; revise; record; audience; explain
notes: Keep a revision log for one piece against shared criteria, recording each change and the date, then share the finished piece with an audience and say how it shows the student's aim. What changes: changes are kept over time and shown as growth, where grade 3 kept a change list. Assessed by a portfolio entry with before and after versions, shared with an audience with its intent explained, scored on a rubric.

words: timing; pitch; form; time signature; notation; culture
cross_subject: math:4.NF.A.1 (equal note values, such as two quarters in one half)
notes: Mark the rhythm, pitch and form of a piece the class will perform, read and play it from picture or standard notation, and explain how its social and cultural setting shapes how it is sung or played. Equal note values are shown as equal parts of a bar. What changes: elements are named and explained, and setting is explained rather than described. Assessed by a marked score and form map, a read-and-play task and a short explanation, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: interpretive choice; tone color; loudness; speed; intent; explain
notes: Plan the loudness, speed and tone color of a song on an expression map and perform it, then explain how a recorded performer's choices carry the music's meaning. What changes: tone color joins loudness and speed, and explaining replaces describing. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a rubric.

words: solo; group; shared criteria; interpretation; genre; manners
notes: Judge group and solo takes with a shared checklist, rehearse to fix accuracy and expression, and perform alone or in a group with the interpretation and manners the setting and genre call for. What changes: interpretation is tied to the genre, where grade 3 tied manners to the venue. Assessed by a performance, a take judged on class criteria and a self-check, with performer and audience manners observed, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a solo or doubled version is always offered.

words: technical skill; setting; context; reflect; choose; explain
notes: Choose a piece for the class to perform and argue for it (interest, what the class can play, where it will be heard), and tell what in the student's own experience the pick reflects. What changes: the child's own technical skill is a reason for choosing, where grade 3 weighed setting. Assessed by a listening-log entry with a reason scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; element; culture; criteria; explain; connect
notes: Listen to a piece, describe how its form, elements and social or cultural setting shape the response, score it with set criteria and say whether it fits its setting, and link it to another art or subject. What changes: explaining replaces describing: the child says why the setting changes the response. Assessed by a listen-and-explain response scored on a short rubric. words: evidence; interest; skill; setting; context; choose

words: evidence; history; culture; criteria; setting; connect

words: ready; criteria; creator; intent; stage presence; dress

words: criteria; choose; purpose; setting; interest; experience

words: variation; theme; chord progression; phrase; contrast; form

words: unity; variety; variation; chord sequence; notation; audio

words: style; form; criteria; feedback; unity; variety

words: ready; class criteria; style; creator; intent; venue

words: contrast; program; shared criteria; compare; interest; choose

words: sort; compare; setting; teacher criteria; contrast; connect

words: tension; release; balance; expanded form; unity; variety
notes: Notate a piece in an expanded form that plans tension and release while keeping unity and variety, with rhythm phrases, melody phrases and a chord sequence. words: technique; justify; polish; tension; release; balance
notes: Revise a piece with criteria the student picks (technique, style, form, sound sources), justify the final polish against them, and present the notated piece. words: sight-read; treble staff; bass staff; compare; build; effect

words: program; reading; back; evidence; interpretation; convey

words: own criteria; style; culturally authentic; honor; venue; ready

words: program; own criteria; mix; select; interest; contrast

words: program; compare; own criteria; setting; evidence; connect

words: draft; binary; cyclical; one-part; develop; motif

words: criteria; final version; medium; context; share; intent

words: analyze; form; style; mood; aural; model

words: own criteria; compositional technique; medium; context; final version; justify

words: abstract; extended; sonic experience; sketch; multiple; represent

words: complex form; extended; analyze; draft; develop; demonstrate
notes: Develop extended ideas through dated drafts in moderately complex and complex forms, and analyze in an annotated log how the material grew. What changes: complex forms, and analysis where level 2 explained. Assessed by an annotated draft log scored on the Level 3 rubric.
