Level 1 bridge: the first unit teaches the grade 8 techniques and words Level 1 needs, as readiness, and claims no grade 8 id (at most 12 days in the full year, 6 on the 80-day short path, STANDARD.md 3.2).

words: playwright; director; designer; actor; convention; audience
notes: Map how designers, playwrights, directors and actors depend on one another, rehearse and rework a scene with standard staging conventions, and perform a script for an audience the group chooses. What changes: the roles of a production are named and a script is staged for an audience. Assessed by a staged showing with a rehearsal record, scored on a short rubric for role, revision and fit to the audience.

words: given circumstances; script; believable; authentic; technique; response
notes: Build a character from the script's given circumstances, work on varied acting techniques, test body, voice and physical choices for believability, and keep script notes on the character. What changes: the script is studied for the character's circumstances. Assessed by a performed character study with a rehearsal log, scored on a short rubric for believable choices and a stated reason for each. Teacher note: no real weapons, no contact stage fights and no rehearsed falls.

words: technology; research; impact; emotional pull; production element; design
notes: Research how a technology changes design choices, use researched tech elements in a production design, refine it so it serves the story's mood, and reflect on how a show's elements look and feel. What changes: research and technology now shape the design, where grade 8 only refined the plan with simple technology. Assessed by a design folio with a short written defense, scored on a short rubric for concept, research and fit to the story. Teacher note: props are checked before use, and no real weapons or flames appear on stage.

words: relationship; research; root; cultural; social; story
notes: Map how relationships between characters move a story, research how theater artists tell stories, and research a play's cultural and social roots. What changes: relationships carry the story and research gives it roots. Assessed by a research note and a staged excerpt, scored on a short rubric for sources, structure and a clear claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: belief; culture; era; setting; view; choice
notes: Write a dramaturgy page on one play: how its culture, local ideas and the student's own beliefs shape it, how belief systems of other times and places shaped similar choices, and which cultural views could change how it is judged. What changes: the student compares belief systems across cultures, places and eras. Assessed by a written reflection and a class discussion, scored on a short rubric for evidence, range of viewpoints and respect. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: criteria; response; decision; experience; justify; taste
notes: Draft criteria for judging artists' choices from what was seen and heard, compare choices artists made from personal experience across several works, and justify the student's own taste. What changes: criteria are formed from the student's own response. Assessed by a response essay or journal entry using evidence from a play, scored on a short rubric.

words: evidence; criteria; purpose; audience; history; appreciation
notes: Analyze a drama piece with evidence and criteria, tie it to other arts, history and culture, and weigh its purpose and intended audience. What changes: the study is tied to other arts, history and culture. Assessed by a written critique with evidence and criteria, scored on a short rubric.

words: custom; concept; sharpen; history; culture; look
notes: Research how past and cultural customs shape a production's look, and sharpen a concept in a portfolio page that shows how history and culture shaped it. What changes: the student shows which customs shaped the concept and sharpens it. Assessed by a concept portfolio entry with sources, scored on a short rubric for research, a stated concept and a reason. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Level 2 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: interpret; team; concept; rehearsal; process; audience
notes: Agree as a team on how to interpret a drama work, use rehearsal to test the concept and the tech design, and present for a chosen audience in a way the process shaped. What changes: the team makes interpretive choices and rehearsal tests the concept. Assessed by a staged showing with a rehearsal record, scored on a short rubric for role, revision and fit to the audience.

words: script detail; research; vision; choice; experience; revise
notes: Keep a character file that marks the script clues, research and director's vision behind each choice, then revise body and voice choices in rehearsal from that file and the student's own experience. What changes: research and the student's own experience shape the character. Assessed by a performed character study with a rehearsal log, scored on a short rubric for believable choices and a stated reason for each.

words: concept; convey; rethink; production knowledge; reading; feeling
notes: Solve design problems with what the student knows of stage technology, design a production that conveys a concept, revise it in rehearsal to strengthen the story's mood, and interpret the play while respecting others' readings. What changes: the design must carry the production's concept. Assessed by a design folio with a short written defense, scored on a short rubric for concept, research and fit to the story.

words: distinctive; lasting; research; bias; belief; decision
notes: Analyze what makes a drama work believable and lasting, let research on a topic shape the student's creative choices, and check how the student's own bias may skew the findings. What changes: research is checked for the student's own bias. Assessed by a research note and a staged excerpt, scored on a short rubric for sources, structure and a clear claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: mirror; challenge; cross-cultural; blend; insight; interpret
notes: Choose and interpret a play that mirrors or challenges the student's beliefs, blend practices from other arts and subjects into a cross-cultural piece, and use a drama work to learn about a culture. What changes: the student picks the play and blends several arts. Assessed by a written reflection and a class discussion, scored on a short rubric for evidence, range of viewpoints and respect. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: reading; criteria; proof; standard; debate; taste
notes: Show how different readings of the criteria could change later choices, build evidence and standards for artistic choices, and sort the range of tastes and beliefs seen in drama the student joins or watches. What changes: criteria are read in more than one way and backed with proof. Assessed by a response essay or journal entry using evidence from a play, scored on a short rubric.

words: weigh; communicate; audience; purpose; history; judge
notes: Write a critique that ties a play to other arts, history and culture, and judges how well it reaches its intended audience and purpose. What changes: a play is judged against how well it reaches its audience. Assessed by a written critique with evidence and criteria, scored on a short rubric.

words: blend; convention; form; tradition; original; concept
notes: Combine dramatic forms, stage conventions and technology in a production concept, and build an original play idea from analysis, research and traditions from more than one part of the world. What changes: the student blends forms and traditions into an original concept. Assessed by a concept portfolio entry with sources, scored on a short rubric for research, a stated concept and a reason. Level 3 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: style; genre; form; transform; production; research
notes: Develop interpretive choices as an ensemble for a devised or scripted work, reshape it in rehearsal while setting its style, genre and form, and present a production for a chosen audience, drawing on research from each creative role. What changes: the class invents the style and form of a production and presents it. Assessed by a staged showing with a rehearsal record, scored on a short rubric for role, revision and fit to the audience.

words: technique; source; defend; research; authentic; culture
notes: Prepare one role with several researched acting techniques, choose and defend warm-ups from sound sources, and bring research, script study, history, culture and the student's own experience into one performance. What changes: the student defends techniques with sources and weaves history and culture into the character. Assessed by a performed character study with a rehearsal log, scored on a short rubric for believable choices and a stated reason for each.

words: full design; defend; advanced; aesthetic; production element; concept
notes: Design a full production that uses every tech element, defend each choice by showing how it carries the concept, apply advanced tech skills in rehearsal, and weigh other readings of the same production. What changes: a full design is made and defended. Assessed by a design folio with a short written defense, scored on a short rubric for concept, research and fit to the story.

words: directing concept; director; style; critical; evidence; meaning
notes: Build a directing concept for a play from a study of two directors' styles, test the research behind each choice before using it, and defend a reading of the play's social and historical meaning in a director's note. What changes: the student forms a directing concept and defends it from critically read research. Assessed by a research note and a staged excerpt, scored on a short rubric for sources, structure and a clear claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: global issue; viewpoint; belief; question; insight; setting
notes: Devise with the ensemble a play about a global issue seen from personal, local and cultural viewpoints, question beliefs of different cultures, places and eras, and let what is learned shape the student's response to a play. What changes: the class makes a play on a global issue and questions beliefs. Assessed by a written reflection and a class discussion, scored on a short rubric for evidence, range of viewpoints and respect. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: history; culture; proof; standard; revise; ground
notes: Write a critique that uses history and culture to organize and defend the response to a play, use solid evidence and fitting standards to revise own work and interpret others', and explain the student's tastes as grounds for the research behind artistic choices. What changes: response is organized with history and culture and used to revise the student's own work. Assessed by a response essay or journal entry using evidence from a play, scored on a short rubric.

words: research; history; culture; current issue; debate; artistic choice
notes: Write a critique that uses researched history and culture to back or challenge a play's choices, and debate how the play speaks to current issues for its audience. What changes: researched history backs the judgment and current issues are debated. Assessed by a written critique with evidence and criteria, scored on a short rubric.

model_in: what-if-list; given-circumstances; group-agreements; rehearsal-log; critique-protocol; artist-statement; story-map; script-markup
model_out: what-if-list; given-circumstances; group-agreements; rehearsal-log; critique-protocol; artist-statement; story-map; script-markup
words: directing concept; interpretation; tradition; transform; team; original
notes: The student leads a production concept: a written concept that blends research, tradition and technology, built with a team, tested in rehearsal and reshaped by what the rehearsals show. Assessed by a concept portfolio with a rehearsal record and a defense of each choice, scored on a short rubric with a higher bar for independence. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new, self-chosen work. Level 4 is optional: checkpoints are check days and critique is on respond days.

words: role; technique; source; research; authentic; defend
notes: The student prepares and performs a role of their own choosing, keeps a rehearsal log that names each technique used and where it came from, and defends the choices in a short talk. Assessed by a performed role, the log and the talk, scored on a short rubric for believability and for sources. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to a new role. Teacher note: no real weapons, no contact stage fights, no rehearsed falls.

words: full design; production; audience; defend; aesthetic; technology
notes: The student designs and presents a production for a chosen audience, with a full design folio, advanced tech used in rehearsal and a written defense that weighs another reading of the same show. Assessed by the production (staged or recorded), the folio and the defense, scored on a short rubric for design, fit to the audience and a reasoned defense. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to the student's own new work. Teacher note: public domain, openly licensed or student-written scripts only, and no flashing lights; a showing outside class needs a yes. A student of 18 or over gives their own yes to be shown; otherwise the family does.

words: critique; proof; standard; history; culture; issue
notes: The student writes a researched critique of a play of their own choosing, using history and culture to organize the response and stated standards to back it, and revises their own work from what the critique showed. Assessed by the written or recorded critique with sources, scored on a short rubric for evidence, standards and fairness. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new works.

words: global issue; research; belief; critical; setting; meaning
notes: The student writes and researches a short play or scene on a global issue, reads the research critically to defend choices, and defends a view of the play's social and historical meaning. Assessed by the researched script or excerpt with a source note and a discussion, scored on a short rubric for sources, range of viewpoints and respect. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to a new project. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: move; idea; music; picture; travel; stay still
notes: Dance to music, pictures and objects, and try new ways to travel and to stay in place while changing one element of the dance, such as speed or size. What changes: first year, play with a starting point and one change. Assessed by a teacher observation of a short free-movement turn, marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: children dance in a clear space and a child may watch first.

words: inspire; starting point; travel; in place; element; try
notes: Move to a starting point such as a poem, a picture or a sound and tell what sparked the moves, then make travelling and in-place moves change by changing one dance element (speed, level or size). What changes: children name the source of an idea and change an element on purpose. Assessed by a short showing and a spoken line about the starting point, scored on a three-line guide.

words: idea; source; link; move; change; element
notes: Make moves from a starting point and name other places dance ideas can come from, then link several different moves into a phrase while changing one dance element. What changes: ideas are gathered from more than one place and linked. Assessed by a short linked-moves showing and a list of idea sources, scored on a three-line guide.

words: choose; challenge; solution; own idea; show; pick
notes: Pick a starting point of the student's own and make moves from it, then solve a movement challenge set by the teacher and show the chosen solution. What changes: children choose their own starting points and solve a challenge. Assessed by a showing of one chosen solution with a one-line reason, scored on a short rubric.

words: choreography; inspiration; invent; challenge; element; solve
notes: Collect choreography ideas from music, pictures and experiences on an idea card, then set a movement challenge for a partner that is solved by changing dance elements. What changes: children invent the challenge, not only solve one. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the challenge, the solution shown or filmed, and a short note, scored on a short rubric.

words: story; nature; news; material; several; build
notes: Build dance material from several sources (a story, nature, a news item), and set and solve a few movement challenges with a small group. What changes: more than one source feeds one body of material. Assessed by a movement-material portfolio entry scored on a short rubric for variety and a stated source.

words: alike; opposite; style; connect; choreography; express
notes: Join ideas from different inspirations by what they share or how they clash to build a short dance, and try movement styles to turn those ideas into steps. What changes: ideas are joined by likeness or contrast, and styles are tried on purpose, where grade 5 gathered material from several sources. Assessed by a short dance idea showing and a written note on the styles tried. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: compare; broaden; range; expressive; aim; dance terms
notes: Compare several sources of inspiration and use the chosen ones to widen the student's moves and range, then pick movement styles that fit the aim and explain them with dance terms. What changes: choices are compared and defended with dance words. Assessed by a showing plus a short written or spoken reason using dance terms, scored on a short rubric.

words: study; inspiration; favorite; original; justify; style terms
notes: Turn several sources into movement material for a dance study, then choose the student's own strongest moves for an original dance and justify them with style terms. What changes: the dancer owns the material and defends the picks. Assessed by a portfolio entry of the study and a justification, scored on a short rubric.

words: stimulus; strengths; demanding; original; analyze; test
notes: Try many sources of movement for one piece of choreography and analyze in the process log how each shaped it, then test dance elements to find the student's strengths and choose demanding moves for an original piece. What changes: analysis of how a stimulus shaped the piece. Assessed by a portfolio entry with a short analysis, scored on a short rubric. Level 1 bridge: the first unit teaches the grade 8 techniques and words Level 1 needs, as readiness, and claims no grade 8 id (at most 12 days in the full year, 6 on the 80-day short path, STANDARD.md 3.2).

words: combine; invented; established; style; purposeful; compare
notes: Choreograph a dance that combines invented and established movement from gathered source material, blending the student's strengths with more than one style, and compare the approach with that of known choreographers. What changes: styles are blended and choreographers are compared. Assessed by a dance portfolio entry and a short comparison, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: any dance of a community is studied from its own published teaching or a named practitioner first. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. Level 2 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: voice; risk; intent; habit; surprising; stretch
notes: Make a dance that carries a stated intent from blended sources, taking risks to find a personal voice, then push past usual movement habits for surprising solutions and explain in the log how they strengthened the intent. What changes: risk and a personal voice, with the reasons stated. Assessed by a portfolio entry of a risk-taking piece and a defended explanation, scored on the Level 3 rubric. Level 3 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: improvise; start; middle; finish; feeling; move
notes: Improvise a short dance with a start, a middle and a finish, and show a feeling or idea in spontaneous movement alone or with a partner. What changes: first year, a three-part shape and a feeling. Assessed by a short showing marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: a child may dance with a partner or beside the teacher.

words: sequence; improvise; choice; feeling; music; talk
notes: Improvise a short sequence with a start, middle and finish and say why you made one choice, and pick moves that show a feeling or follow a bit of music. What changes: the child talks about a choice, where kindergarten only danced a three-part shape. Assessed by a showing and a spoken line about one choice, scored on a three-line guide.

words: phrase; central idea; ending; mood; justify; clear
notes: Improvise a phrase whose middle holds the main idea and that ends clearly, and give a reason for choosing moves that show an idea, mood or music. What changes: a central idea sits in the middle and the ending is clear, with a reason for the moves chosen. Assessed by a short phrase showing and a spoken reason, scored on a three-line guide.

words: pattern; AB; ABA; form; tool; phrase
notes: Use choreographic tools such as repetition and reversal to make simple patterns and AB and ABA forms, and make a phrase that shows a feeling or idea, then talk about how the choices worked. What changes: named forms and tools replace free improvising. Assessed by a performed AB or ABA phrase and a short discussion, scored on a short rubric.

words: alter; tool; option; form; study; main idea
notes: Change choreographic tools (repeat, reverse, add a level) to open up pattern and form choices, and build a dance study around one main idea, then discuss how well the choices worked. What changes: tools are changed on purpose and the study has a main idea. Assessed by a performed study and a short written or spoken evaluation, scored on a short rubric.

words: expand; communicate; without words; chosen moves; tools; study
notes: Alter several choreographic tools together to open up options and sharpen the main idea, and build a study from chosen moves while talking about how dance says things without words. What changes: several tools are changed together and the student reflects on how the study means something, where grade 4 altered tools for one study. Assessed by a performed study and a short reflection scored on a short rubric.

words: purposeful; goal; criteria; personal; cultural; judge
notes: Build a dance study toward a goal you set, using choreographic tools and forms, and write criteria for a personal or cultural study to judge which moves say it best. What changes: the study has a stated goal and the student's own criteria, where grade 5 built a study around a main idea. Assessed by a performed study plus a criteria sheet scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: shape; vary; criteria; meaning; explain; study
notes: Shape a dance study with several tools and forms and explain the choices, and write criteria for a personal or cultural study that say how it carries its meaning. What changes: criteria are defined and explained, where grade 6 wrote and applied them. Assessed by a performed study and a written explanation scored on a short rubric.

words: together; new dance; group; process; apply; effect
notes: With a group, choose tools and a form for a new dance and keep a note on how the group worked, then write criteria for a personal or cultural dance and use them on the piece. What changes: the work is made with others and the group process is described, where grade 7 made a study alone. Assessed by a group performance and a process description, scored on a short rubric.

words: collaborate; structure; purpose; artist's statement; support; elements
notes: Make a dance with others whose structure serves its purpose, and write an artist's statement on how structure and elements support it. What changes: a written artist's statement joins the making, where grade 8 only defined criteria. Assessed by a performed dance and its written statement, scored on a short rubric for structure, purpose and reasons.

words: original; design; composition; aesthetic; statement; analyze
notes: Make original dances alone and with others, analyze how their structure serves their purpose, and write a statement of the student's aesthetic to guide later choices. What changes: a personal aesthetic is stated and composition is analyzed, where level 1 wrote about one dance's purpose. Assessed by a portfolio entry of a dance with an aesthetic statement, scored on a short rubric.

words: fluency; personal voice; heighten; viewpoint; cultural; justify
notes: Choreograph original dances with a personal voice, justify the choices that sharpen the purpose, and write a statement of the student's own cultural and artistic viewpoint. What changes: fluent original work and a viewpoint stated. Assessed by a portfolio of original dances and a defended statement, scored on the Level 3 rubric. Teacher note: a student names only a heritage they choose to name; no one is asked to represent a group.

words: change; guide; improvise; draw; move; symbol
notes: In a guided improvisation, change a move when the teacher suggests a new way, and draw a picture or symbol for one move. What changes: first year, try a change and draw a move. Assessed by a teacher observation of one changed move and a drawn symbol, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: suggestion; remember; sequence; picture; symbol; jump
notes: Try a suggested change in an improvisation and in a short remembered sequence, and draw pictures or symbols for moves such as jump, turn and slide. What changes: a remembered sequence is changed and moves get symbols. Assessed by a changed sequence and a page of move symbols, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: choice; high; middle; low; level; recalled
notes: Try choices and suggestions that change a remembered sequence or improvisation, and draw symbols for high, middle and low levels. What changes: the child draws levels as symbols and chooses a change, where grade 1 drew move types. Assessed by a showing of a changed sequence and a level drawing, scored on a three-line guide.

words: feedback; alter; describe; route; map; direction
notes: Change moves in a short dance after partner feedback and say what changed, and chart the phrase's directions and paths on a floor map with symbols. What changes: feedback drives a revision and a pathway map is made. Assessed by a revised phrase, a one-line description of the change and a route map, scored on a short rubric.

words: classmates; comment; reflection; intent; relate; beside
notes: Rework a dance after classmates' comments and the student's own reflection to sharpen its intent, and sketch where dancers stand in relation to each other (beside, in front, behind, above). What changes: comments and the dancer's own reflection both drive the rework, and relationships between dancers are drawn. Assessed by a revised piece, an explanation of choices and a relationship sketch, scored on a short rubric.

words: peer; suggestion; widen; refine; log; video
notes: Try peer suggestions to open up choices in a short dance and explain the changes kept, and log what changed in the sequence in words, drawings or a recording. What changes: a change log is kept as the work grows. Assessed by a revised piece and its change log scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no student is recorded, photographed or filmed without the family's yes; a face or voice is never required (hands, the work or the sound alone will do); a student who does not want to be recorded is observed live and the teacher's mark stands; kept work stays on the student's, family's or school's own device.

words: criteria; group; revise; fit; own method; write down
notes: Revise a dance against criteria your group built and explain how each revision fits the intent, and invent your own way of writing down a sequence of moves. What changes: the group builds the criteria and the student invents a way to record moves, where grade 5 logged changes. Assessed by a revised dance and a written sequence in the student's own method, scored on a short rubric.

words: judge; adjust; standards; notation; established; record
notes: Weigh possible revisions, adjusting the student's own standards when needed, and explain how they make the intent clearer, then try an established notation method to record a sequence in writing, signs or a recording. What changes: revisions are judged against shifting standards and a real notation method is studied. Assessed by a revised dance and a notated sequence, scored on a short rubric.

words: alone; collaborative; excerpt; strengthen; part; notation
notes: Revise choreography alone or with others against criteria and feedback and explain how the changes strengthen the intent, and record a dance excerpt with parts of an established notation method. What changes: the revision is independent or shared and an excerpt is notated. Assessed by a revised piece and a notated excerpt, scored on a short rubric.

words: devices; structure; evaluate; compare; notation; section
notes: Rework a dance's devices and structure to make its purpose clearer and judge what the changes did, and compare two established notation methods by recording one section in each. What changes: devices and structure are reworked, and notation methods are compared, where grade 8 tried one method on an excerpt. Assessed by a revised dance with an evaluation and a notated section, scored on a short rubric.

words: refine; criteria; feedback; strategy; media; plan
notes: Refine a dance's devices and structure against criteria and feedback and judge the student's own revisions, and plan how to record the whole dance with notation or media. What changes: a recording plan covers a whole dance, where level 1 notated a section. Assessed by a refined dance and a recording plan, scored on a short rubric.

words: document; justify; reflection; complete; notation; record
notes: Refine devices, structure and criteria through reflection and feedback, log and defend each revision, and record a complete dance with an established notation method. What changes: a whole dance is notated and every revision is defended, where level 2 only planned the recording. Assessed by a portfolio entry of the revision record and the notated dance, scored on the Level 3 rubric.

words: shape; line; level; size; tempo; quick
notes: In a group circle, make shapes with straight and curved lines at high and low levels and big and small sizes, match speed to the drum, and move in quick, floppy or sharp ways. What changes: space, time and energy meet as three simple ideas, with no dance elements named before. Assessed by a short movement task marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: this unit names the elements and does not drill the motor skill, which physical education teaches.

words: path; zigzag; curved; beat; slow; bouncy
notes: Change shape, level and facing, travel on curved and zigzag paths in lines and circles, move at three speeds to a steady beat, and name the qualities danced, such as bouncy or floppy. What changes: paths, speeds and quality words are named, where kindergarten only showed shapes and sizes. Assessed by a movement task with a spoken quality word, scored on a three-line guide.

words: direction; symmetrical; phrase; strong beat; circle; turn
notes: Dance a short study with clear directions, symmetrical and uneven shapes, short and long phrases and landings on the strong beat in two- or three-beat music, tell circling from turning, and choose quality words to dance. What changes: phrase length and strong beats are heard and shown, where grade 1 kept a steady beat. Assessed by a movement task and a quality word, scored on a three-line guide.

words: space; dimension; focus; phrasing; dynamics; energy
notes: Dance with a sense of distance and all three dimensions, shape filled and empty space with focus, improvise to fill a set count while keeping the music's timing, and change energy to give moves a clear quality. What changes: the dancer judges distance and timing alone, where grade 2 followed set directions. Assessed by a short improvised performance scored on a short rubric for space, time and energy.

words: fixed; changing; rhythm; percussion; tempo shift; analyze
notes: Make still and changing shapes with eye contact between dancers, play a simple drum part for others to dance to, move to steady and uneven rhythms and react to tempo shifts, and describe energy changes in vivid words, then refine the phrase. Land jumps softly. What changes: irregular rhythms are answered and energy is described in words, where grade 3 stayed with the music's timing.
